**Gødstrupklyngen** is a healthcare cluster (sundhedsklynge) operating within [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] in Denmark [^src5]. It serves as a key organizational unit in the national clinical quality development program for [[atrieflimren|atrieflimren]] (atrial fibrillation), monitored by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP). The cluster's performance is systematically tracked across multiple clinical quality indicators, ranging from anticoagulation treatment coverage and diagnostic echocardiography to the incidence of stroke, severe bleeding, and mortality.

In terms of clinical performance, Gødstrupklyngen has demonstrated strong results in specific areas of early intervention. Notably, it is highlighted as one of the health clusters that successfully meets the national standard for Indicator 1, which measures the timely initiation of anticoagulation therapy for newly diagnosed patients, achieving a result of 92.9% [^src1]. However, the cluster faces documented challenges in long-term treatment persistence; it is identified as one of only four clusters—alongside [[klynge-syd|Klynge SYD]] and [[klynge-nord|Klynge NORD]] in Region Nordjylland, and [[sundhedsklynge-sydvestjylland|Sundhedsklynge Sydvestjylland]]—that fails to meet the standard for [[indikator-4a3|Indikator 4a3]] (5-year treatment coverage) [^src12]. 

Furthermore, Gødstrupklyngen is included in comprehensive geographic and epidemiological analyses across the Danish healthcare system. For instance, it is part of the national mapping of stroke incidence ([[indikator-5|Indikator 5]]) among atrial fibrillation patients at the health cluster level [^src4]. Its data is consistently reported in the annual "Atrieflimren i Danmark" reports (2024 and 2025), providing detailed metrics on patient outcomes and enabling regional benchmarking and targeted quality improvement initiatives [^src2] [^src6] [^src7] [^src8] [^src9] [^src10] [^src11].
